summary: Loader shim silently imports sibling scoped package on require
details: index.js is a verbatim copy of the feross/buffer library with an added top-level dynamic import of the sibling package @vaultflow/create-flow whose returned promise is assigned to a variable and never referenced. Any consumer that require()'s @vaultflow/update-flow, advertised as a buffer/streaming utility, triggers in-process loading and execution of @vaultflow/create-flow's module code as a side effect. The package's identity signals are also mismatched: package name is @vaultflow/update-flow, repository is github.com/guilderguzman/sql-link, keywords are [node, sql], README describes bare-stream and instructs `npm i @sql-access/nods`, while the shipped code is the buffer library. The combination is consistent with a disposable loader shim in a multi-package chain, where the actual payload lives in the sibling package pulled in by the side-effect import.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
